name: Domo
description: Domo is a cloud-based data and analytics platform that connects 1,000+ data sources, builds BI dashboards and embedded analytics, and adds AI agents and workflow automation on top of a governed data foundation, billed on a credit-based consumption model.
best_for: Companies that want one platform combining data integration, BI dashboards, embedded analytics, workflow automation, and AI agents, billed on usage-based credits with unlimited users rather than flat per-seat licenses.
features: Connects 1,000+ data sources into a single governed data foundation
Drag-and-drop ETL and a low-code app builder for building custom BI tools
Dashboards, visualizations, and embedded analytics for sharing insights inside or outside the organization
Domo AI: custom AI agents, AI chat, model management, and AI-readiness tooling built on top of connected data
Workflows, alerts, and scheduled reports for automating recurring business processes
Credit-based consumption pricing with unlimited users and no per-seat charges
SSO (SAML/OIDC), multi-factor authentication, IP restrictions, and Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) encryption for enterprise governance and security
pros: Unlimited users at every level — cost scales with credit consumption, not headcount
30-day free trial includes full platform access and unlimited users, with no credit card required
Domo states current certifications including SOC 1, SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27018, HIPAA, HITRUST, GDPR, and CCPA on its own trust page
cons: No published numeric pricing at all — becoming a paying customer requires booking a demo/contacting sales rather than a self-serve checkout
Credit-based consumption pricing (charged for actions like storing data, updating tables, or running workflows) can be harder to estimate upfront than a flat per-seat plan

pricing.starting_price: No published numeric price; Domo uses custom, credit-based consumption pricing available only by booking a demo/contacting sales after the free trial

tiers.name: Free Trial
tiers.notes: 30 days, no credit card required. Full platform, unlimited users, onboarding support, self-service education, and one training session.

tiers.name: Custom Pricing
tiers.notes: Credit-based consumption pricing — credits are consumed for actions like storing data, updating tables, running workflows, or ML inference. Unlimited users at every level. Requires booking a demo/contacting sales. Adds a dedicated account team, volume discounts, custom add-ons, support packages, AWS PrivateLink, and an optional HIPAA-compliant environment.

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.description: A BI and data-visualization platform licensed by role (Viewer/Explorer/Creator) rather than Domo's unlimited-user, credit-based consumption model.
alternatives.best_for: Teams centered on deep, ad hoc visual analytics who are comfortable with per-role licensing instead of a broader connected data/workflow/AI platform.
strengths: Dedicated authoring apps for Windows and Mac

alternatives.name: Microsoft Power BI
alternatives.description: Microsoft's BI platform, priced per user rather than by consumption credits, with deep Microsoft 365 and Fabric integration.
alternatives.best_for: Organizations already standardized on Microsoft 365 that want simple published per-user BI pricing rather than Domo's broader, consumption-billed data/AI/workflow platform.
strengths: Large existing installed base within Microsoft shops

faq.question: Does Domo have a free plan?
faq.answer: Domo doesn't have a perpetual free plan, but it offers a 30-day free trial with full platform access, unlimited users, and no credit card required.

faq.question: How is Domo priced?
faq.answer: Domo uses credit-based consumption pricing: credits are consumed for actions like storing data, updating tables, running workflows, or using ML inference. There's no published numeric rate — pricing is custom and requires booking a demo or contacting sales.

faq.question: What compliance certifications does Domo have?
faq.answer: Domo states its current certifications include SOC 1, SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 27018, HIPAA, HITRUST, GDPR, and CCPA, according to its own trust and security page.
